newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks shed 3.43pct, seen correcting.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks shed 3.43pct, seen correcting.

text.p: The Athens bourse fell 3.43 percent on Wednesday as construction and bank shares continued their fall on lighter volume. Market watchers said a correction had been expected.

"This drop was expected after the market's recent volatility. Most good news had been discounted by the bourse a long time ago and fresh news are needed for it to rise again," said Nikos Lainas, investment manager at Aspis Investment .
Such good news were banks' good 1997 profit forecasts and expectations on Athens' candidacy to host the Olympic Games of 2004 which had been discounted some time ago, he said.
Improved macroeconomic figures and strong first semester company results as well as good dividend news could drive the bourse higher after its interim correction, he added.
The general share index will trade between 1,150 and 1,250 points in the short term, he said.
Another broker said he had been expecting a milder correction.
"A correction was expected but not such a sharp one. However, I am not alarmed. It could be mutual funds lightening up on positions," said broker George Molyviatis, at Pegasos Securities.
The Athens general share index closed 3.43 percent or 44.59 points lower at 1257.00 points from Tuesday's 1301.59 after opening at 1294.90. The session's low was at 1250.72.
Turnover dropped to 12.5 billion drachmas on volume of 3.8 million shares. Decliners led advancers 187 to 35 with 16 issues unchanged on 238 traded.
Construction fell 4.13 percent, banks dropped 4.60 percent and investment shares closed 4.61 percent down. Industrials settled 2.81 percent lower. Small caps lost 2.08 percent.
